answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, with escrowed bonds slashed when an arbitrator verifies fraud. Whether agents sell onyx, umber pigment, or karst survey data, every active identity needs its own bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize $100,000 and risks losing the bonds used for fraud; creating more names cannot bypass that capital requirement.
